name: Testosterone

track.title: Label update
track.line: Feb 2025: TRAVERSE and blood pressure added

track.title: Compounded forms
track.line: Creams and sprays: not FDA approved

what.text: Testosterone is the main male sex hormone. It is a steroid made mostly in the testes. Testosterone cypionate is a longer-acting form, an ester of testosterone, given into the muscle.
How it acts, according to the FDA labels:

items.text: It drives the growth of the male sex organs and keeps up male traits such as body hair, a deeper voice, muscle and fat distribution.
In many tissues it works after being converted to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which binds receptors inside cells.
Androgens have been reported to raise red blood cell production.
Testosterone taken from outside the body shuts down the body’s own signal (LH) to make testosterone. At large doses it also shuts down FSH, which can suppress sperm production.

what.text: Adonis carries testosterone in three forms: creams applied to the skin, sprays, and testosterone cypionate given by injection. The creams and sprays are compounded products. They are not FDA approved. We could not confirm whether Adonis’s cypionate injections are the FDA-approved product or a compounded version.

research.text: Testosterone has been studied in large randomized trials. The largest, TRAVERSE, followed 5,246 men for about three years and looked at heart safety. It did not test whether testosterone helps symptoms. Each study is listed below as it was run.

research.title: TRAVERSE: heart safety, 2023 (USA)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter. Built to show testosterone was not worse than placebo for heart events (noninferiority). Funded by AbbVie and others.
5,246 men aged 45 to 80 with heart disease or high heart risk, symptoms of low testosterone, and two fasting testosterone levels under 300 ng/dL
daily 1.62% testosterone gel or placebo gel
mean treatment 21.7 months; mean follow-up 33.0 months
first heart attack, stroke or death from heart causes (MACE)

research.found: MACE occurred in 7.0% of the testosterone group and 7.3% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.96). Testosterone met the noninferiority test. Atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury and pulmonary embolism were more common with testosterone.

research.meta: USA · 2024 · Sub-study of a randomized trial
research.title: TRAVERSE fractures sub-study, 2024 (USA)

facts.v: sub-study of TRAVERSE; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
clinical fractures, checked against medical records

research.found: Fractures occurred in 3.50% of the testosterone group and 2.46% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 1.43). Testosterone did not lower fractures.

research.title: Testosterone Trials in older men, 2016 (USA)

facts.v: randomized, placebo-controlled; three linked trials (sexual function, physical function, vitality). Funded by the National Institutes of Health and others.
790 men aged 65 or older with testosterone under 275 ng/dL and symptoms
sexual activity and function, walking distance, fatigue, mood

research.found: Sexual activity, desire and erectile function scores rose more on testosterone. Mood and depressive symptom scores were slightly better. There was no difference in vitality (fatigue score), and no difference in walking distance in the physical function trial itself. The authors said the trial was too small to judge risks.

research.title: Testosterone and sperm production, 1990 (WHO)

facts.v: multicentre study of testosterone injections as male contraception. No placebo group.
up to 6 months to suppress sperm, then a 12-month phase

research.found: 157 men stopped producing sperm in three semen samples in a row. After injections stopped, the median time back to a normal sperm count was 3.7 months.

items.text: FDA reviewed TRAVERSE and, in February 2025, told makers of all testosterone products to add its results to their labels and remove Boxed Warning language about a higher risk of heart outcomes. FDA kept the statement that use for age-related low testosterone is not established.

src.label: FDA class-wide labeling changes for testosterone

items.text: The labels say safety and efficacy in men with “age-related hypogonadism” have not been established.
The Depo-Testosterone label says the drug has not been shown to be safe and effective for improving athletic performance.

us.text: Testosterone is an FDA-approved medicine for men with low testosterone caused by a medical condition (hypogonadism). It is a Schedule III controlled substance. The compounded creams and sprays Adonis carries are not FDA approved. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: FDA lists the first US approval of testosterone as 1953. Approved forms include gels, a patch, a buccal system, oral products and injections.

src.label: FDA class-wide labeling changes for testosterone

items.text: approved in 1979 under application ANDA 085635. It is approved for replacement therapy in men with primary hypogonadism or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
AndroGel 1% was approved in 2000 and AndroGel 1.62% in 2011, for the same two kinds of hypogonadism in adult men.
use in men whose testosterone is low only because of age (“age-related” or “late-onset” hypogonadism), and use in males under 18 (AndroGel). Use outside the labeled conditions is off-label.
topical testosterone gels carry a boxed warning for secondary exposure. Children have developed male traits after touching unwashed or uncovered skin where a man applied gel.

on February 28, 2025, FDA told makers of all testosterone products to add TRAVERSE results, remove the Boxed Warning language about higher heart-outcome risk, and add or update warnings that testosterone can raise blood pressure. FDA said blood pressure studies confirmed an increase class-wide.

src.label: FDA class-wide labeling changes for testosterone

items.text: yes. Testosterone, with its salts and esters, is a Schedule III anabolic steroid under federal law.

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.
This applies to the testosterone creams and sprays Adonis carries. We could not confirm whether Adonis’s testosterone cypionate injections are the FDA-approved product or compounded.

world.lead: Testosterone is an authorised prescription medicine for hypogonadism in the US, Canada, the UK and the EU. It is a controlled drug in the US and Canada. It is banned in sport at all times.

countries.status: Approved medicine (e.g. Depo-Testosterone, AndroGel) for hypogonadism. Prescription-only; Schedule III controlled substance.
Authorised medicine (AndroGel 1% pump, marketed). The database lists Depo-Testosterone as a controlled drug (CDSA Schedule IV) and its 100 mg/mL product as cancelled post-market (July 2025).

after.text: Australia’s Poisons Standard (June 2026) lists testosterone in Schedule 4 (prescription-only) and in Appendix D, clause 5, for anabolic and androgenic steroids. Under that clause it must not be possessed without authority under local law. We could not reach the TGA’s register to confirm which products are registered.

In 2014 the EU’s CMDh, after a PRAC review, found no consistent evidence of a higher heart risk in men with hypogonadism, and asked for warnings that low testosterone be confirmed by symptoms and lab tests before treatment.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Testosterone is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition) under class S1, anabolic agents, on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List, when given from outside the body. It is a non-Specified Substance. We could not open the 2027 list to check for changes.

side.text: The labels list serious risks, including blood clots, higher blood pressure, higher red blood cell counts, worsening prostate symptoms and lower sperm production. Gels can pass testosterone to children and women by skin contact.

items.text: at large doses, testosterone can suppress sperm production through feedback on FSH, lowering sperm count. Oligospermia (low sperm count) may occur. Subfertility, infertility and testicular shrinkage are reported with abuse.

children exposed to a man’s gel have had genital enlargement, pubic hair, more erections, aggressive behavior and advanced bone age. In a few cases changes did not fully reverse. Women can develop male traits. Testosterone can harm a female fetus.

src.label: MHRA Drug Safety Update, topical testosterone

items.text: in a blood pressure monitoring study, AndroGel 1.62% raised average blood pressure by 1.9/1.3 mm Hg after 16 weeks, and by 3.0/2.2 mm Hg in men on blood pressure drugs. Testosterone is not recommended with uncontrolled high blood pressure.

items.text: heart attack, stroke and heart death were similar (7.0% vs 7.3%). Non-fatal arrhythmias needing treatment (5.2% vs 3.3%), atrial fibrillation (3.5% vs 2.4%), acute kidney injury (2.3% vs 1.5%) and bone fracture (3.5% vs 2.5%) were more common with testosterone.
items.lead: Heart and kidney events in TRAVERSE:

items.text: deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism have been reported. In TRAVERSE, clots occurred in 1.7% on testosterone vs 1.2% on placebo.
higher hemoglobin and hematocrit (polycythemia). The labels say to check these periodically.
worsening of an enlarged prostate and a possible risk of prostate cancer. Not for men with breast or known or suspected prostate cancer. Breast growth (gynecomastia) may develop.
fluid retention and swelling, sleep apnea, lipid changes, liver effects with long high-dose use of some androgens, acne, mood changes, and changes in libido.

abuse at high doses has been linked to heart attack, heart failure, stroke, liver damage and serious psychiatric effects. Stopping after high doses can cause withdrawal symptoms such as depression and fatigue.
pain and inflammation at the injection site. The cypionate injection contains benzyl alcohol, which has been linked to serious reactions in newborns.

unconfirmed: We could not confirm whether the testosterone cypionate injections Adonis carries are the FDA-approved product (such as Depo-Testosterone) or a compounded version. The creams and sprays are compounded and not FDA approved.
The Drugs@FDA website blocked automated access; approval dates come from FDA’s own Drugs@FDA data through openFDA.
Australia’s TGA register (tga.gov.au) could not be reached, so we could not confirm which testosterone products are registered there. Only the Poisons Standard scheduling is reported.
MHRA’s product register needs JavaScript and could not be read. The UK status comes from an MHRA Drug Safety Update only.
We could not open WADA’s 2027 Prohibited List, so any 2027 change is not reported.
Canada’s Controlled Drugs and Substances Act text (Justice Laws) could not be opened. The CDSA Schedule IV status comes from Health Canada’s product database.
surprises: FDA removed Boxed Warning language about a higher risk of heart outcomes in February 2025, after TRAVERSE. But it also required new or updated warnings that testosterone raises blood pressure, and the label now lists more atrial fibrillation, kidney injury, clots and fractures on testosterone than placebo. The trial does not support either “testosterone causes heart attacks” or “testosterone has no heart risks.”

Every label checked says safety and efficacy in “age-related” low testosterone have not been established, and the EU says restoring levels in healthy older men is not an authorised use. Testosterone is often marketed for aging men.
Testosterone from outside the body suppresses sperm production. WHO tested weekly testosterone injections as a male contraceptive. It does not raise fertility.
In the TRAVERSE sub-study, fractures were more common on testosterone (3.50% vs 2.46%), not less, despite common claims that it protects bones.
Health Canada’s database lists Depo-Testosterone 100 mg/mL as cancelled post-market in July 2025.
